clue.text: Short of time, whip round with snack

indicators.note: the trimmed whip goes round the other piece, enclosing it
being short of something means lacking it, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: a switch is a thin whip or cane
and means with, joining things together

explanation.surface: Pressed for time, someone passes the hat round to pay for a quick bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip round' reads as a collection of money, but 'whip' and 'round' work separately: one is a synonym, the other the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandwich is the classic light meal eaten on the go, a typical example of a snack.

clue.text: My soup is cooked before mass meeting

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged letters ahead of the mass abbreviation
cooked means doctored or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Soup is prepared ahead of a big gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like it belongs to the soup in the surface, but it signals rearranging the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A symposium is a conference or formal meeting for discussing a subject.

clue.text: We fail completely to get here fast

definitions.meaning: to make no progress at all
split as two words, it reads ...: come here at once

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two words, a command to come here immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting nowhere is the idiom for failing completely, and split in two it reads as a call to come here right away.

clue.text: 5 ac was one, bridge partners declare

parts.note: in bridge West and East are partners
the second of the partnered pair
to aver is to declare or assert

explanation.surface: A clue about a figure who sat at a bridge table and declared.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom (5 across) is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream. In bridge, West and East play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Bottom in A Midsummer Night's Dream is a weaver by trade, so this names his profession.

clue.text: Carrier containing writer's chips?

indicators.note: containing means the carrier word holds the writer inside

parts.note: a carter carries goods by cart
a pen is a writer, as in a hired pen

explanation.surface: Someone carrying a writer's potato chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' is the nickname for a carpenter, from the wood chips; the question mark marks the nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips is a traditional nickname for a carpenter, especially a ship's carpenter, from the wood shavings he makes.

clue.text: Last cargo vessel?

definitions.meaning: a ship's hull below the waterline, and by extension a ship itself, the part that carries the cargo

explanation.walkthrough: In shipping a bottom is the hull and so a merchant ship; the question mark flags that slightly stretched sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming bottom means finishing last, and bottom is an old word for a cargo ship's hull or the ship itself.

clue.text: Prickly hazard bachelor encountered on walk

indicators.note: in a down clue, the bachelor letter sits on top of the walk

parts.note: a ramble is a leisurely walk

explanation.surface: A single man meets a thorny obstacle while out walking.
explanation.definitionFit: A bramble is a thorny blackberry bush, a prickly hazard to walkers.

clue.text: Expressing admiration for water feeder

definitions.meaning: an adjective for paying tribute or homage
a stream or river that flows into a larger one

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the rarer adjective, paying tribute.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means paying tribute, and as a noun it is a stream feeding a larger river.

clue.text: Row about small room shaped like an eye

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the row word goes round the room

parts.note: to row is to oar
a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over a small eye-shaped room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it means to propel with an oar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocellar means relating to an ocellus, a simple eye or eye-like spot, so eye-shaped.

clue.text: Flyer at coast somewhere? Not so, here

indicators.note: the word not tells us that the following words are to be absent from the one before

parts.note: taken as written; the clue removes two named words from it, and the remaining middle run is a coincidence of that deletion, not a hidden word
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where a seabird lives: by the sea somewhere, but apparently not around here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes SO and HERE from SOMEWHERE, leaving the three middle letters. 'Somewhere' looks like part of the definition, but it is the word being cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: The mew is the common gull, a seabird seen flying along the coast.

clue.text: It stimulates a backward idiot to acquire a trade

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word for idiot in reverse

parts.note: a nerd is a foolish or socially inept person
taken as written
a line is a line of work, a trade or business

explanation.surface: A drug that stimulates even a slow-witted person enough to learn a trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns NERD into DREN; 'to acquire' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenaline is the hormone that stimulates the body, raising heart rate in the fight-or-flight response.

clue.text: Alert old writer taking the old press chief about

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: about means around, so the editor's letters go around the old article

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper
ye is the archaic form of the

explanation.surface: A veteran writer stays watchful while bringing the former newspaper boss around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press chief' is the editor, a standard crossword convention; 'taking' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open-eyed means watchful and fully aware, a synonym for alert.

clue.text: Trinket British union leader put back in package

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the package word

parts.note: a bale is a large bound package of goods

indicators.note: put back means the letters are reversed in order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A British trade union boss hands back a trinket in a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union leader' gives U; with B, 'put back' turns BU into UB, and 'in' sets it inside BALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bauble is a cheap showy ornament, which is what a trinket is.

clue.text: I went to law for tree

parts.note: taken as written
lex is the Latin word for law, used in legal phrases

explanation.surface: Someone takes legal action over a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: LEX is Latin for law, familiar from phrases like lex talionis.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the holm oak, and also the botanical name of the holly genus, so it names a tree.

clue.text: Live with Greek historian, not entirely hating foreigners

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase defining a noun for a person who hates foreigners

indicators.note: not entirely means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Xenophon was the Athenian historian who wrote the Anabasis
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Living with an ancient Greek historian who partly hated foreigners.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition loosely describes the person by his attitude; 'with' joins the pieces in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: A xenophobe is a person with an irrational fear or hatred of strangers and people from abroad.

clue.text: Staff takes elaborate care to secure southern plant

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast inside, so the charade encloses the southern letter

parts.note: a stave is a staff or stick

indicators.note: elaborate means worked out in detail, signalling the word care is reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Office staff take great care to protect a plant from the South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees, but it is a stick; the southern letter sits at the join of the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Stavesacre is a larkspur whose seeds were used as a poison against lice, so it names a plant.

clue.text: Express anger, caught in this bloody pump!

parts.note: to vent is to express, as in venting feelings

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for caught is placed within the irritation word

parts.note: to rile is to anger
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone vents fury about their wretched heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express anger' reads as one idea but gives two pieces; 'this' merely points to the defined organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventricle is one of the heart's chambers that pumps blood out, so a pump full of blood.

clue.text: Staying power of Parisian in French river

parts.note: en is French for in, as a Parisian would say
the Durance is a river in south-east France

explanation.surface: Someone from Paris shows stamina swimming in a French river.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is French for in; the Durance flows into the Rhone near Avignon.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity to keep going, which is exactly what staying power means.

clue.text: It motivates mother early in the year

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
spring is the early season of the year, so early in the year is in spring

explanation.surface: Something gets a mother moving at the start of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainspring is the chief driving force behind something, what motivates it, from the spring powering a clock.

clue.text: Wither, left over in new-mown hay

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the scrambled hay
freshly cut, signalling the hay is chopped up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: over in a down clue tells us to turn the word upside down

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Something withers when left lying in freshly cut hay.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' is a natural reversal signal; 'left' looks like a verb, but it is the side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To atrophy is to waste away or wither, as unused muscles do.

clue.text: Hair treatment required for inside function

indicators.note: inside means the word for is placed within the hair treatment

parts.note: a perm is a hairdressing treatment that curls the hair

explanation.surface: A hairdo is needed for an indoor social function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' looks like a noun, a social occasion, but it is the verb: to perform is to function.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform is to function or work, as in a machine that performs well.

clue.text: Distance cart has to be reversed

indicators.note: to be reversed tells us to write the word for cart backwards

parts.note: a dray is a low heavy cart, as used by brewers

explanation.surface: A cart has to back up some distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard is a unit of length, three feet, so it is a measure of distance.

clue.text: A bogus journalist hanging his head

parts.note: sham means fake or bogus
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A fake reporter is caught out and hangs his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging one's head is the posture of shame, so it pictures someone who feels ashamed.

clue.text: Look for male member of the Anatidae family

definitions.meaning: to have a ... is British slang for to take a look

definitions.text: male member of the Anatidae family
definitions.meaning: the Anatidae are the duck and goose family, and the male goose has its own name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a gander' is British slang for take a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A gander is a male goose, a member of the duck family, and gander is also slang for a look.

clue.text: Appropriate description of name someone's given

definitions.meaning: suitable or right for the occasion
a personal name like Mary or London is a ... noun, as opposed to a common one

explanation.walkthrough: In grammar a proper name or proper noun is one given to a particular person or place.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means fitting or suitable, and a proper noun is a name given to a particular person.

clue.text: One spreads the message by crossing part of river

indicators.note: crossing here means straddling, so the word for by sits on either side

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
a reach is a straight stretch of a river

explanation.surface: Someone spreads the word by fording a stretch of river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' here means spanning, so the word for 'by' sits on both sides of the river stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher delivers sermons, spreading the religious message to a congregation.

clue.text: Decided a month back he for one was to lead

indicators.note: was to lead puts the grammatical piece in front of the month

parts.note: he is an example of a pronoun

indicators.note: back tells us to write the month abbreviation in reverse

parts.note: DEC is short for December

explanation.surface: Someone decided a month ago that he would take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DEC into CED; 'was to lead' puts PRONOUN first.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronounced as an adjective means marked or definite, as in a pronounced limp, so it means decided.

clue.text: Crew needing long hair cut short

indicators.note: cut short means losing the last letter

parts.note: a mane is a long thick head of hair

explanation.surface: A ship's crew whose long hair needs a trim.
explanation.definitionFit: To man a ship is to crew it, supplying the people who work it.

clue.text: Lecture-hall chimney lined by unknown engineer

indicators.note: lined by means the chimney has the other letters along its inside

parts.note: lum is a Scottish and northern word for chimney
Y is a mathematical unknown
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: A lecture hall whose chimney was lined by an anonymous engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: LUM is a Scots and northern English word for chimney, rarely met outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyceum is a hall for public lectures, named after the Athenian school where Aristotle taught.

clue.text: Envy possession of book, say, by Barnaby

parts.note: say gives EG, for example
Barnaby Rudge is the Dickens novel and its title character, so Barnaby points to his surname

explanation.surface: Someone envies a person who owns a Dickens novel such as Barnaby Rudge.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnaby Rudge is a novel by Charles Dickens; Barnaby leads to the surname RUDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge someone something is to resent or envy them for having it.
